### J-1 Deleting "the SVGs the previous run listed" trusts a file anyone can edit
- quote: "delete only the SVGs the previous run listed as its own and no longer draws"
- situation (adversary): the list lives in explainer.md, which humans and agents edit and merge. A line like `../../src/logo.svg`, or an absolute path, makes the re-run delete a file outside the spec folder. A list lost in a merge leaves orphans, or lets a run delete nothing without saying so. AC-33 only covers a clean list and a sibling `notes.svg`.
- fix: say deletion is limited to `.svg` files directly inside the explainer's own folder; any other entry is ignored with a warning.
- validation: confirmed: FR-26 limits deletion only to "SVGs the previous run listed", and the list sits in the editable explainer.md; no requirement bounds the path, and AC-33 tests only a clean list plus a sibling file.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q4: delete only own-prefixed listed SVGs in the explainer folder, never drill-down SVGs, warn on other paths (FR-26, AC-33)

### J-2 Topic name goes straight into a file path
- quote: "write `.nio/research/<date>-<topic>-explainer.md`, with its SVGs beside it"
- situation (adversary): the human asks to explain "../../.claude/settings" or "a/b", or gives an empty, very long or non-ASCII topic. The spec has no slugging rule, so the write lands outside `.nio/research/` or fails with a half-written file. FR-27 "continue that file" then appends to whatever file that path matches, and two different topics can collide on one slug and merge silently.
- fix: add an FR that turns the topic into a safe slug (charset, length cap, non-empty), always inside `.nio/research/`, and says what happens on a collision between different topics.
- validation: confirmed: spec-adversary: FR-14 now slugs the topic, caps it at 40 characters and refuses an empty result, which closes the path escape. The collision half of the fix asked is still open. Two different topics can reduce to the same 40-character slug on the same date, and FR-27 "continue that file" then merges them silently. No requirement says what happens then (for example, record the original topic in the file and refuse or suffix on mismatch).
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q10: topic text stored; a clash with a different topic writes -explainer-<n>.md and says so (FR-27, AC-35)

### J-3 A config value can make the check pass without checking anything
- quote: "skip rendering and the check's diagram checks with a note"
- situation (adversary): `explain.format` is set to any host skill name, or the skill name is mistyped but still present on the host. `nio check explainer` then skips "the check's diagram checks", so a plan explainer with no component map and no build order exits 0. AC-10 keeps core-diagram and contract-ID checks when only Node is missing, but FR-20 and AC-27 do not say they stay. The pass is silent apart from one note line.
- fix: keep the core-diagram and contract-ID checks for every format (they need only the file's headings and labels). Skip only render and syntax checks.
- validation: merged: same as J-13

### J-4 The 20-node cap is a rule nothing enforces
- quote: "THE SYSTEM SHALL keep every diagram at or under 20 nodes."
- situation (adversary): the agent draws a 60-node diagram, or a drill-down section adds one. FR-8 fails only for a render failure, a missing core diagram or a missing contract ID, so `nio check explainer` passes. AC-5's observable counts nodes, but only in an e2e run on the agent's own output, and no check fails on it. The "one huge diagram" misuse in UJ-1 therefore goes unrejected.
- situation (testability): AC-5's Observable only counts nodes, so "answers one question" is never tested. `nio check explainer` (FR-8) fails only on render, missing core diagram or missing contract ID, so a 25-node diagram passes the check and only the e2e agent run would catch it. How a "node" is counted (subgraph boxes? edge labels?) is not defined.
- fix: add "a diagram block over 20 nodes" to the FR-8 failures, or state that the cap is advisory.
- validation: confirmed: FR-7/NFR-1/AC-5 (Level: e2e) set the 20-node cap, but FR-8 (line 176) fails only on render, missing core diagram or absent contract ID. Nothing says the cap is advisory, and "node" counting is undefined.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q6: check fails a diagram over 20 distinct node IDs (FR-7, FR-8, NFR-1, AC-5)

### J-5 Rendering runs an unpinned fetched package on text derived from untrusted input
- quote: "Rendering through `npx` fetches and runs a third-party package"
- situation (adversary): the Risks section names this, but no requirement or AC limits it. An unpinned package, or a typosquatted or compromised one, runs on every machine that renders, and `nio check` runs the same path. Diagram text comes from spec and topic text. Mermaid labels or directives such as `click` and HTML labels end up in a committed SVG that humans open in a browser. Nothing pins the version, escapes labels, or says what happens when the network is down; the last case may be read as "Node not available" and quietly give text-only output.
- fix: add an FR that pins the renderer version, sanitises labels or uses Mermaid strict mode, and separates "network or fetch failed" from "no Node", with a visible note for each.
- validation: confirmed: The Risks section names the npx fetch, but no FR or AC covers version, label handling, or a failed fetch; FR-11 only covers "Node is not available", so a network failure is unspecified.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q7: one exact mermaid-cli version; notes tell no Node from fetch failure; only a broken diagram fails (FR-9, FR-11, AC-14)

### J-6 Host-skill format may skip the contract-ID check that FR-8 requires
- quote: "skip rendering and the check's diagram checks with a note"
- quote: "a plan contract ID is absent from the component map's node labels"
- quote: "check exit 0 with a note naming the format"
- situation (consistency): `explain.format` names a host skill and the plan's CT-3 is missing from the component map labels. FR-20 says the check skips "the check's diagram checks", and the contract-ID check is one of the FR-8 checks, so the check may pass with exit 0 even though FR-8 says it must fail naming CT-3. The spec does not say whether the contract-ID check is a "diagram check".
- fix: name the checks that a host-skill format skips (render only, or render plus core-diagram plus contract-ID) and state which one stays on. If the contract-ID check must still run, say how it reads labels from a non-Mermaid explainer.
- validation: confirmed: FR-8 lists the contract-ID check as a failure, FR-20 skips "diagram checks" without defining them, and AC-27 expects exit 0 with only a note; the spec leaves the CT-3 outcome open.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q5: host skill skips rendering only; core, contract, node-cap and walk-through checks still run; FR-20/21 now human (FR-20, FR-21, AC-27, AC-28)

### J-7 Core-diagram check may fail every topic explainer
- quote: "a core diagram is missing"
- quote: "apply the component-map contract-ID check to plan explainers only"
- quote: "an overview diagram, then one per drill-down section"
- quote: "always include a component map and a build order diagram in a plan explainer"
- situation (consistency): a topic explainer has only an overview diagram and drill-down diagrams, with no component map or build order. FR-15 limits only the contract-ID check to plan explainers, so the other FR-8 checks read as applying to topic explainers too. Read that way, `nio check explainer` on a topic explainer fails with "a core diagram is missing" every time. AC-20 covers only the contract-ID check, so nothing says the core-diagram check is off for topics.
- situation (logic): a topic explainer holds an overview diagram and drill-down diagrams (decision table row `topic`), with no component map or build order. FR-2 requires core diagrams only in a plan explainer. FR-8 fails any explainer with "a core diagram missing", and FR-15 excludes only the contract-ID check. AC-20 expects "no contract finding" and says nothing about the core check. The outcome for a topic explainer is therefore pass or fail depending on how FR-8 is read. The command is also `nio check explainer <slug>`, and a topic explainer has no slug, so how it is named to the check is unstated.
- fix: state in FR-8 or FR-15 that the core-diagram check, like the contract-ID check, applies to plan explainers only, and say what topic explainers are checked for.
- validation: confirmed: FR-8 fails on "a core diagram is missing" with no mode scope and FR-15 scopes only the contract-ID check; the Glossary says core diagrams are present in a plan explainer but never says the check skips topic explainers.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-15/AC-20 scope core-diagram and contract checks to plan explainers (FR-2 already scoped core diagrams to plan mode); a topic explainer is checked by path, render only

### J-8 Staleness is said to follow the plan, but FR-16 also fires on spec.md and contracts.md
- quote: "a changed plan flags it stale but"
- quote: "The plan changes after the explainer was written."
- quote: "WHEN spec.md, plan.md or contracts.md changed or is gone since its explainer was written"
- quote: "print `stale: explainer.md (plan changed)`"
- situation (consistency): spec.md changes, and FR-16 says the explainer is stale. The fixed status text still reads "(plan changed)", which is not true when only spec.md changed. The Summary and UJ-4 speak only of the plan.
- fix: either change the trigger to the plan (and drop spec.md and contracts.md from FR-24 and FR-16, which AC-31 also relies on), or make the printed text name the source that changed.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: Stale line reworded to 'spec, plan or contracts changed' (FR-16, AC-21); spec.md as a source was an agent call in the delegated grill (OP-3), shown to the human

- quote: "each marked as written for an earlier plan"
- situation (consistency): the Decisions line says drill-down sections are kept "marked for review". FR-25 and AC-32 say they are marked "as written for an earlier plan". An implementer who follows the Decisions line writes a different marker, and AC-32 would fail on it.

### J-10 Flow output "same with and without the explainer" conflicts with suggesting explain
- quote: "`nio flow next` output is the same with and without the explainer"
- quote: "WHEN the plan gate closes as approved THE SYSTEM SHALL suggest `@nio:explain` in `nio flow next`."
- situation (logic): the plan gate is approved. Case 1: no explainer, so FR-18 and AC-24 require `nio flow next` to name `@nio:explain`. Case 2: explainer written, so AC-23 requires identical output, meaning it still suggests explain forever. If it stops suggesting, AC-23 fails. If it keeps suggesting, the flow nags after the step is done, and UJ-4's "the stale line goes away" has no matching "suggestion goes away".
- fix: state that the suggestion shows only while no explainer exists, and reword AC-23 to compare only the blocking or gating parts of the output.
- validation: confirmed: AC-23's Observable says `nio flow next` output is the same with and without the explainer, while FR-18 and AC-24 require it to name `@nio:explain` after approval; both cannot hold once an explainer exists unless the suggestion never goes away.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: AC-23 Observable excepts FR-18's suggestion; no flow guard refuses for the explainer

### J-11 Re-run keeps drill-down sections but deletes the SVGs they show
- quote: "keep every drill-down section below them, each marked as written for an earlier plan"
- quote: "delete only the SVGs the previous run listed as its own and no longer draws"
- situation (logic): a plan explainer has a drill-down section on component CT-2 with its own diagram and `drill-ct-2.svg`, listed as the previous run's. The plan changes and explain re-runs. FR-25 keeps the section, which still references `drill-ct-2.svg`. The re-run redraws only the core and flow diagrams, so it "no longer draws" that SVG and FR-26 deletes it. The kept section then points at a missing image.
- fix: say whether drill-down diagrams and their SVGs count as the re-run's own. Either exempt SVGs referenced by kept sections from deletion, or say kept sections lose their images.
- validation: confirmed: FR-25 keeps drill-down sections while FR-26 deletes SVGs the re-run "no longer draws"; the spec never says whether kept drill-down sections' SVGs count as still drawn, so images can be deleted from kept sections.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q4: delete only own-prefixed listed SVGs in the explainer folder, never drill-down SVGs, warn on other paths (FR-26, AC-33)

### J-13 Host-skill row skips "diagram checks", which may include the core and contract checks

### J-14 Re-run marks drill-down sections "earlier plan" even when the plan did not change
- quote: "WHEN a plan explainer is re-run THE SYSTEM SHALL redraw its diagrams and keep every drill-down section below them, each marked as written for an earlier plan."
- situation (logic): the plan did not change and the human re-runs explain. FR-25 has no change condition, so every drill-down section is marked "earlier plan" although it matches the current plan. The mark also cannot tell a section marked in run 2 from one written in run 1 after run 3, as nothing says whether the mark repeats or stays.
- fix: apply the mark only when the recorded source hashes (FR-24) differ from the current ones, and say that an existing mark is not duplicated.
- disposition: spec-fix by agent: FR-25 marks sections only when a source hash differs from the recorded one; matches the human's Q1, which was about out-of-date re-runs

### J-15 One spec bundles several separable features
- quote: "A new skill, `@nio:explain`, turns an approved plan into `explainer.md`"
- quote: "It can also explain a topic or an implementation"
- quote: "### US-8 Choose the diagram format (P3) [human]"
- situation (scope): the plan explainer (US-1, US-2), the SVG render path (US-3), topic mode (US-5), the stale flag (US-6), the flow suggestion (US-7) and the format switch (US-8) are gated as one unit with 27 FRs. A slice that only writes a plan explainer and checks it cannot be approved, or can be built, without also waiting for the render, topic and format work. The spec names no epic and no slice order beyond the P1/P2/P3 tags.
- fix: split into an epic with slices, for example plan explainer and check (P1), then render, then topic mode and drill-down, then stale flag and format switch. Or state in the spec why one spec is kept.
- validation: refuted: Template permits a single spec (epic field is optional), and the stories already carry P1/P2/P3 priorities and an Independent test each, which is the slicing the spec uses; no rule or grill answer demands a split, so this is a preference, not a defect.

### J-20 "Short" walk-through has no number
- quote: "each followed by a short walk-through"
- situation (testability): the Observable says "each followed by prose". A one-word line or a 2,000-word essay both pass, so the test cannot fail if FR-6 ("short plain-language") breaks.
- fix: give a limit (for example, 1 to 8 lines or at most 120 words per walk-through) and state it in the Observable.
- validation: confirmed: spec-testability: FR-6 and AC-1's Then clause now give 1 to 120 words, but AC-1's Observable still says "each followed by prose". An e2e run with a 0-word or a 2,000-word walk-through still passes the Observable. The pack shows no AC with a fixture whose walk-through is over 120 words that the check must fail. Put the limit in the Observable, or add an integration AC like AC-5's.
- disposition: spec-fix by grill: Human Q11: AC-36 proves a 121-word walk-through fails the check
